claims.text: Under elevated-temperature, high-shear loading, FeNiCrCoCu coating wear resistance is governed by formation of an ultra-nanocrystalline or partially amorphous surface layer.
The transformed near-surface layer reduces friction relative to an untreated coating.
The transformed near-surface layer reduces material removal and wear relative to an untreated coating.
A controlled thermal and high-load pretreatment will promote dynamic surface nanocrystallization or amorphization in FeNiCrCoCu.
High-temperature wear testing itself can promote dynamic surface nanocrystallization or amorphization in FeNiCrCoCu.
Thermal activation combined with mechanical shear induces grain refinement or dynamic amorphization.
The ultrafine transformed layer redistributes applied loads more effectively.
Load redistribution by the transformed layer hinders microcrack initiation and propagation.
Hindering microcrack initiation and propagation reduces friction and wear.
Pretreated or high-temperature-tested FeNiCrCoCu coatings will contain a measurable nanocrystalline or amorphous near-surface layer.
Pretreated or high-temperature-tested coatings will have lower friction coefficients than as-deposited coatings tested under milder or room-temperature conditions.
Pretreated or high-temperature-tested coatings will have lower wear rates than as-deposited coatings tested under milder or room-temperature conditions.
The proposed mechanism operates effectively at approximately 300–500 °C under high-load wear.
Excessive oxidation or phase instability outside the proposed operating limits may interfere with formation of the transformed surface layer.
In CoCrFeMnNi, low friction and wear have been linked to an ultra-nanocrystalline near-surface layer and a dynamic-amorphization model.

contradictions.description: The predicted outcome compares pretreated or high-temperature-tested coatings with baseline coatings tested at milder or room temperature, confounding pretreatment with test temperature. The falsification experiment instead tests both pretreated and as-deposited sets at 300–500 °C.
